Pre-2.0 hardening — the shortlist

Analysis·seedling·proposed·JUL 19, 2026

The bug/reliability work worth landing before the 2.0 tag, triaged by one rule: 2.0's story is agent-face + self-healing daemons + honest UI, so fix what undermines that. Features and render polish defer past the tag.

Contents

  • Tier 1 — block the tag
  • Verify & close
  • Tier 2 — land after Tier 1
  • Tier 3 — close the recurrence (bit us this campaign)
  • Deferred past 2.0

Triage rule: fix what undermines the 2.0 story (the agent face, self-healing daemons, honest UI). Defer features and render polish past the tag.

Tier 1 — block the tag

Issue Why it blocks The fix
#1334 + #1375 prod-safety. An agent /be run disrupted production kolu.service; a local vitest forked 30+ daemons and OOM-reaped prod kaval. Running kolu’s dev on kolu can kill prod — the only dangerous class here. A tooling-level guard (PR #1338, a prod-guard justfile recipe) was already tried and closed unmerged. One PR, three locks in the product: (a) any dev/test run that spawns daemons is forced into a private throwaway state-root — the harness refuses to start against the real one; (b) the production service marks its daemons, and every dev-side adopt/kill/discover path refuses a marked daemon, loudly; (c) the test harness runs its children under a process+memory cap, so a fork-bomb starves itself, not prod. #706 is the same class; its full leg (VM/container containment) stays deferred.
#1859 In simple words: one corrupt message makes the wire reader report “this connection is over” — but it never actually stops reading. Every later message is still decoded and delivered into a peer the server already closed and stopped counting. A zombie connection: bookkeeping says dead, socket says alive. On settle, detach the 'data' listener; on decode failure, destroy the stream — so “the read promise settled” and “the read actually stopped” can never diverge (stdio-codec.ts:126-135). Audit links/stdio.ts for the same divergence.
#1754 claude-code live state can lie: stuck “thinking” after the turn completed, never reconciling. A lying dock guts the observe-out UX. Reproduced — CI evidence on aarch64-darwin (ollama fast turns: 2.88s turn, indicator stuck thinking for the full 60s), and four real-agent e2e scenarios sit descoped waiting on it. Two known mechanisms, both in the issue: the transcript watcher attaches after the turn’s JSONL landed and only tails (fix: initial full-scan on attach), and deriveState maps only stop_reason === "end_turn" to waiting (fix: reconcile the emulated stop reasons). Landing both restores the descoped e2e asserts — the regression pin comes free.
#1177 awaiting_user doesn’t chime when the prior state was waiting — they’re one attention class, and the alert only fires on entering the class. Badge always shows; sound is timing-dependent. If 2.0 sells “agents that ping you,” this must work. Draft PR #1894 (reproduce-first RED, then a 3-refuter design gate): an attention-episode latch — ≤1 chime per notify-class run, episode ended only by a work state; trigger = class-entry OR escalation into the fenced awaiting bucket; honest “needs your input” copy.
#1763 boot wedge — a fresh load intermittently sticks at “Connecting to local…” and terminal-create wedges. The scopedByEntry non-member warn was ruled out (benign per-boot transient); the live wedge did not reproduce across a fault-injection campaign. Mechanism pinned (code-grounded, on the issue): the connect overlay is held by any of three loading legs but its only timeout escape is coupled to the daemon leg — a hung membership leg (no activeScope() ⇒ the anchor is never stamped) or a hung session/terminalKeys leg has no escape at all. Fix: one boot deadline anchored at app start, outside the per-host scope, escaping on any stuck leg — gated on the fault-injected repro in the issue’s §5.

Verify & close

Issue The facts
#1681 was Tier 1; isn’t anymore. PR #1687 (merged 2026-07-05) reproduced the real mechanism — a boot-window per-key get threw, killing the chip’s subscription non-retriably — and fixed it. No recurrence reported since. Confirm in the field, close; the spellability residual is #1688 (deferred with reasoning).
#901 kaval’s survivor architecture is this feature: PTYs live in kaval, and a kolu-server redeploy does not touch them — shipped behavior. Confirm, close.
#1793 closed during this audit — fixed by merged #1892 (presence-only dialogs).
